pr_title: fix(es/minifier): Mark `delete` as a property mutation

issue_context.title: Compress is using deleted properties with `"sourceType": "module"`
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Compressing code with `"sourceType": "module"` can result in using properties in conditions **after** they are deleted.


This is a very trimmed-down example of code running in `jQuery` (there's also a playground link). It may be encountered within other libraries as well.
Example from `jQuery`:
There is a variable initialized reading properties at the start of the function that is used in checks later.:
```javascript
function defaultPrefilter( elem, props, opts ) {
	var prop, value, toggle, hooks, oldfire, propTween, restoreDisplay, display,
		isBox = "width" in props || "height" in props, // <-- the important line in this example
	...
```
Those properties are then deleted:
```javascript
for ( prop in props ) {
    value = props[ prop ];
    if ( rfxtypes.test( value ) ) {
        delete props[ prop ]; // <-- the properties are deleted here, so reading them later will not yield anything
...
```
Then the variable is checked:
```javascript
if ( isBox && .... ) { // <-- there result of the property check is stored in `isBox` is it does not matter that the properties are now deleted
...
```

When compress is enabled, the variable at the start of the function is omitted and the property check is used in the condition instead after the property is deleted:
```javascript
if ( ("width" in props || "height" in props) && .... ) { // <-- properties are deleted, so the check will never pass here
...
```

I have attached a playground link. 
If the source type is set as `script` the variable is kept instead, which will result in the correct behavior. 
With source type `module` the variable is omitted and checking deleted properties will result in conditions never passing.

### Input code

```typescript
const props = {'a': 1, 'b': 2};

const isBox = 'a' in props || 'b' in props;

for (const p in props) {
    delete props[p];
}

console.log(isBox);
```



### Playground link

https://play.swc.rs/?version=1.3.4&code=H4sIAAAAAAAAA0vOzysuUSgoyi8oVrBVqFZPVLdSMNRRUE8C0ka11rxcvFzJYCWZxU75FUAlQBUKmXlQHTU1IJVwPlh5Wn6RggZETwFcRlOhmpeLMyU1J7UkFSISXRALVF4LsyA%2FJ1UvJz9dA2yNpjUAuvuWq5cAAAA%3D&config=H4sIAAAAAAAAA22TQZbbMAiG7%2BJ1Fm0Xs5gDdNcz6CkScphKwk%2BgTPzycvciJ5bjpDvzGRD8wHX4Yjd8XofJFobSvnjOYi%2FD5wAuWXYFJxluh0FsGUEa5l8%2Ffn4MhyFhxjC3EEdpKsDcvtWtJsiiRrCR4aCk0LeaUqpaR6IINr%2FZxrLBLDBC2UIdxWgnBnO2pUe012xBprxDVcCbqdD0RLNHQcqabGUerDeOPHSABZzgGTYXzaEumbWwXskCPRzrODaZ7p5wtrFa6bngssigL%2Fa4EyGLCTXzC9pVekf3Jh9eGEwBqSWvPl%2BEeafDXwCtM1rmbBNskQsPOoe9Z%2FiPF%2BagQ5S500hPVWUYtTmDGHqHrWoogptaBXx10Dp0W%2FIH3DXE6MFACKp2D%2BZvFHfaksk8AYVuqmo2bDO4m2bdpz1tK%2FAGf2tV8jyOB09WTq%2BM53Sk%2BJYigZzIv2EVQugVFt3ey%2FRKa%2FagMoN%2F%2BlG5mX1NdfhCJrb7WnXWhdAYM0Y69vW93ZYJ8SqJmol8bWt6XbRbzvOjnet6nOs28Z%2BH45LnHznJfvz3AwAA

### Expected behavior

Ideally, we should not use properties that get deleted a few lines above. If that's even possible to check for.
Source type `module` and `script` should result in the same behavior. 

### Actual behavior

With source type `module` the variable is omitted and checking deleted properties will result in conditions never passing.
If the source type is set to `script` the variable is kept instead, which will result in the correct behavior. 

### Version

1.3.4

### Additional context

_No response_
comments: This closed issue has been automatically locked because it had no new activity for a month. If you are running into a similar issue, please create a new issue with the steps to reproduce. Thank you.

review_comments: I think this is only catching `delete foo.bar`, but fails to capture `delete foo.bar.baz`? Based on the `Expr::Ident(obj) = e.obj` we're inside of. Come to think of it, there are a few others like `foo().bar` that won't be caught?

For `delete foo.bar.baz`, `foo` will be marked as property mutated because we don't unset `is_delete_arg` for the `obj` of `MemberExpr`. ( https://github.com/swc-project/swc/blob/114bc97cf5ba430da4b9561613f4657c9b4afeb8/crates/swc_ecma_minifier/src/analyzer/mod.rs#L1032-L1040 )
And currently, we do not inline properties. But nice catch, we should ensure it when we add partial, per-property inlining.
